payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly present its depicted content as a drawing rather than as an unchanged photograph?
node.criteria: pass: visible rendering establishes a drawing, such as drawn or illustrated forms; fail: the depicted content remains clearly photographic with no visible drawing conversion; unknown: the image does not establish whether it is a drawing or photograph.
node.binding: Assess only whether the image has been rendered as a drawing; do not assess its medium.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image visibly renders the giraffes and surroundings with drawn outlines and a soft, sketch-like appearance rather than retaining the source photograph's photographic rendering.

n3: The node’s own criteria make “complete” require both supports to pass, and both saved supports do pass; the trace is valid, queried, and has no transport or dependency failure. The edited image also visibly has a chalk-like grainy, smudged treatment and drawn outlines, so the evidence does not justify changing either support to fail or treating low confidence as missing progress. The mismatch is instead that the aggregate says “yes” while the reference is “partial.” Clarify the requested-node outcome mapping so that “complete” is not automatically emitted as the aggregate’s yes when the rubric’s partial label applies, and inspect the aggregation/label conversion for this node. Preserve the separate chalk-medium and drawing-form checks and their evidence; do not weaken the completion criterion or invent additional visual requirements to force agreement.
